title: Orbital character and photoemission signatures of the A-pocket in infinite-layer nickelates
authors: Leonard M. Verhoff, Michael Seidl, Liang Si, Karsten Held
abstract: The orbital character of the so-called $A$-pocket in infinite-layer nickelates remains under debate. We investigate bulk NdNiO$_2$ using density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory and identify the $A$-pocket as a strongly hybridized state with substantial interstitial-$s$, Nd-$d_{xy}$ and Ni-d_${xz/yz}$ contributions. Our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy simulations reproduce the main polarization-dependent features measured experimentally. Removing the interstitial-$s$ matrix element leads to a clear disagreement with the measured Fermi surface maps, even though the interstitial-$s$ contribution is not dominant. Suppressing instead the Nd-d$_{xy}$ or Ni-$_{dxz/yz}$ matrix elements leaves the maps almost unchanged, because these are small at the zone corner. More generally, our results demonstrate that assigning the microscopic origin of spectral features in infinite-layer nickelates requires treating orbital hybridizations and photoemission matrix elements together.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the electronic structure and spectroscopic signatures of the A-pocket in nickelates using DFT+DMFT. The authors conclude that the A-pocket arises from strong hybridization among several orbitals, and critically, that the measured photoemission intensity is primarily governed by the interstitial-$s$ orbital's matrix element, resolving previous ambiguities in the field.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing debate regarding the orbital character and physical origin of the A-pocket feature in infinite-layer nickelates.
main_result: The A-pocket is identified as a strongly hybridized state involving interstitial-$s$, $	ext{Nd-}d_{xy}$, and $	ext{Ni-}d_{xz/yz}$ orbitals, with the photoemission signal intensity being dominated by the interstitial-$s$ channel.
method: The study employs Density-Functional Theory combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) to calculate electronic structure, followed by simulating Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) spectra.
model_or_system: The system is infinite-layer nickelates, modeled using a low-energy 11-band tight-binding model incorporating local Hubbard-Kanamori interactions. Calculations are performed for $	ext{NdNiO}_2$ and $	ext{LaNiO}_2$.
key_observables: Orbital character contributions to the A-pocket, polarization-dependent ARPES spectra, and Fermi surface maps.
important_parameters: The hybridization strength between different orbital types (e.g., interstitial-$s$ vs. $d$-orbitals) and the inclusion of local correlations via DMFT.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Plane-Wave Final-State Approximation (PWA) for ARPES simulations, and the $k_z$ assignment in the final-state model is noted as an approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate DFT band structures, orbital projections onto the A-pocket, and simulated ARPES Fermi surface contours for different orbital channels and polarizations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need to treat orbital hybridizations and photoemission matrix elements together. It then uses a full 11-band model to calculate orbital contributions, contrasting these with artificial, decoupled models to pinpoint the dominant physical mechanism governing the ARPES signal.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of orbital hybridization and the explicit calculation of photoemission matrix elements provide a rigorous theoretical framework for interpreting complex spectroscopic features in strongly correlated transition metal oxides.
